To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified genomic alterations specific for stage and MYCN status in NB.
cDNA A-CGH profiling of NBs identified genomic alterations specific for stage and MYCN amplified NBs.
we have identified genomic imbalances that are common and specific to stage and to MYCN amplification in NBs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genomic alterations in neuroblastomas.
the identification of the genomic alterations occurring during neuroblastoma progression.
the identification of genomic alterations in NB and their association with stage and MYCN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MYCN amplified subgroup of NB is a unique entity with specific genomic alterations that distinguish it from the rest of the NBs.
NBs with and those without MYCN amplifications have distinct genomic profiles, and these profiles are further stratified based on stage.
the most frequent genomic alterations in NB are gain of 2 and loss of 1, and that the gain of 17q is common to both MYCN amplified and non-amplified NBs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genomic alterations are not universal for all NBs and the number of genomic alterations required for malignant transformation is less for the Stage 4+ NBs.
the MYCN amplified NBs have the largest amplicons, the Stage 1- and 4- NBs have more frequent alterations, and the Stage 4+ NBs have fewer alterations but they are more specific.
cDNA A-CGH profiling is a valuable tool for the detection of recurrent imbalances, the delineation of amplicons and the identification of single copy number changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most frequent changes in NB occur on 2p, 1p, 3p and 7q.

there are common and unique patterns in genomic imbalance that are associated with the stage and MYCN status in neuroblastoma, which may have implications for the development of targeted therapy for this disease.
the number of genomic alterations required for NB progression is dependent on the risk status of the tumor.
